doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Pay with Bird in Philadelphia and with Lester Young
summary: Money often ran out by week's end in Philly; he made about $96 a week with Lester Young.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Was the money okay when you were working with Bird? I mean, did he . . . he didn’t handle the money? Otherwise you might not have got paid.

When we would play Philadelphia – Bird never stayed in Philly, because he said if he did stay there, he would be arrested. He’d be busted. So he would commute. It would take money to commute. By the end of the week, sometimes there was no money there. The union would be there. The union man would be at a lot of the clubs when we played Philly. We’d be there until almost daylight, waiting to get whatever else was scrambled up. We didn’t make a lot of money in those days, but it was cool enough for me to do what I wanted to do. I made less money with Lester Young. With Lester Young
I made $100 a week, and they took tax out of that. I made around 90 – taxes were very low, maybe 4 or 5 dollars – I made – I got around $96. That wasn’t considered too much, even then.
